context: Checkpoint 2026-08-05. The agent became usable as a daily driver and the record learned to grade it. Proven live on node `sede`, not argued: refarm ask does real tool work through the operator's codex subscription; the observation carries elapsed_ms, a scenario, a verification verdict and a step fraction that matches what the screen printed. The measurement that originated the whole budget laboratory -- 'died at 4/25' -- is recoverable at last. THREE DURABILITY GAPS a new session must know about are listed under blockers.
current_tasks: SHIPPED - the record can say a run was WRONG. refarm.verification.expected/.passed/.method/.unknown, with refarm.outcome untouched: `done` still means the run completed, and correctness is a separate fact. Three states are STRUCTURAL (Matched | NotMatched | Unverifiable(reason), no Absent variant), so an expectation declared but not comparable can never be recorded as a failure. `refarm ask --expect <text>`, substring match, method recorded beside the verdict. Proven live: expect 59 -> passed, expect 9999 -> failed, outcome `done` in both.

SHIPPED - the step fraction, and the 4/25 mystery is solved. steps_completed/steps_planned now count the SAME notion (completion-loop steps) and match the `step N/M` the sidecar prints; the turn count survives as refarm.outcome.turns_completed and travels ALONE, never as half a fraction. Why it looked impossible: a turn is a DISPATCH (one refarm ask = one turn) and nothing declares a max number of turns, so a turn count genuinely has no denominator -- the observation concluded, reasonably and wrongly, that only an AgentPlan could supply one. The 25 was never a plan; it is the react loop's own ceiling, and it always rode on prompt_ref, the same key the observation joins on. A second real off-by-one was found underneath: the loop ran 0..=max_iter, so a ceiling of 25 made 26 completions and would have recorded 26/25. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: MODEL_TOOL_CALL_MAX_ITER=N now makes N completions per dispatch, not N+1.

SHIPPED - work is comparable. refarm.scenario.id (declared, never invented) and .hash (derived from the request shape at dispatch, canonicalised, key-order-stable). Two exclusions were found by MEASURING rather than reasoning: args.replyRef and args.session_id are per-run identifiers, and leaving either in made every run hash uniquely. A fact that is NOT a defect and must not be 'fixed': an agent request is never identical to itself, because ask's system prompt is assembled with DateContextProvider and GitStatusContextProvider. So grouping on the agent path comes from the DECLARED id -- `refarm ask --scenario X` -- not from the hash.

SHIPPED - the node can be restarted safely and says when it is stale. SIGTERM handled like SIGINT (it was not, so every scheduled restart would have been a hard kill), GET /efforts/in-flight, and a drain bounded by the longest in-flight deadline the budget already resolved. Plus two doctor findings: runtime:stale (the running node predates artifacts on disk -- caught the operator's node nine hours behind its own binary while `refarm check` said all-clear) and runtime:bare-environment (a node started without .refarm/.env falls to the keyless local floor and fails only at first use).

SHIPPED - the catalog reaches the node and leaves the crate. 28 verified entries with per-fact provenance, a shadowing guard proven by sabotage, an `unpriced` third state, a managed-file materialiser that updates an untouched copy and KEEPS an edited one, and a crate_boundary test that fails when a production include_str! escapes the crate. Note refarm-tractor is STILL unpublishable for a second reason found by that test: bindgen! reads ../plugin-wit/wit. Recorded, not fixed, in the router spec's D1.

OPEN - cost separation is RECORDED but not QUERYABLE. Every observation already carries host.name, host.id, refarm.workspace.id, refarm.budget.spawner and refarm.cost.estimated_usd -- who ran it, in which workspace, from which surface, for how much. `refarm budget` has exactly ONE subcommand, `observations`. There is no way to ask what rcdc5 cost this month, or what a node spent, or which surface. The operator named cost audit and separation on 2026-08-05 and it is otherwise unmapped.

OPEN - the fourth budget axis, and it governs what the operator ACTUALLY runs. His daily route is openai-codex, a SUBSCRIPTION, so refarm.cost.estimated_usd is honestly 0 and every dollar ceiling measures nothing for the work he does most. The binding constraint is requests per billing period, a quota that REFILLS across runs rather than a ceiling consumed within one. Already specified as a gap in the budget-laboratory design (lines 460-461). Good news measured 2026-08-05: the axis needs no new counter -- observations already carry timestamp_ns and refarm.pricing_mode, so a period's usage is countable from the record the laboratory already keeps.

OPEN - two installers wrote the agent to two directories. `refarm plugin install` writes plugins/refarm_agent/; tractor-start.sh loads plugins/@refarm/agent/ via scripts/agent-install.mjs. The daemon loads the second, so the command the CLI RECOMMENDS on a plugin failure cannot fix it. A fix was in flight at checkpoint time; verify it landed before trusting `refarm plugin install`.
blockers: DURABILITY GAP 1: `.superpowers/sdd/` is GITIGNORED. Fifty-one files and thirty-three subagent reports from 2026-08-04/05 exist only on this machine. Every measurement, every rejected alternative and every 'did not survive contact with the code' finding lives there and in commit messages -- nowhere else. A new session gets the commit messages, which are deliberately thorough for exactly this reason, and nothing more.

DURABILITY GAP 2: there has never been a requirements interview. The operator asked on 2026-08-05 whether his needs are mapped and specified. They are NOT, as a document. What exists is inference spread across specs, docs/CONVERGENCE-LANE.md, and the assistant's own memory in ~/.claude/ -- which lives OUTSIDE the repository and does not travel with the project. Anything a future session knows about what he wants, it knows by reading conversation or by guessing.

The main branch still has NO protection: gh api repos/:owner/:repo/branches/main/protection returns 404. No required PR, no required status checks. GitHub configuration only the operator can apply, and it wants applying before any promotion PR merges.
next_actions: The fourth axis (quota). It governs the operator's actual daily route, needs no new counter, and the budget fold that would carry it is three-level with a hardcoded signature -- 3 Rust callers plus one TS mirror in budget-contract-v1/src/resolve.ts, guarded by conformance. Adding a level is contained but not free, and it is the same fold an automation-scoped budget would later need.

A cost aggregation surface. The axes are already on every observation; what is missing is the question. Smallest honest version: `refarm budget summary --by workspace|node|surface|model` over the record that already exists, with the subscription case reported as quota-consuming rather than as zero dollars, since 0 is true and useless.

The requirements interview the operator asked for. It should produce a document IN the repository, not in assistant memory, and it should be run against what is already built rather than from a blank page -- most of the material exists and is fragmented, which is a different problem from missing material.

What executes a declared automation (spec 2026-08-05, three customers, two of them node-scoped). The declaration language is COMPLETE -- cron, one-shot, event, manual -- and nothing evaluates any of it; no cron parser exists anywhere in the tree. Blocked on nothing but a decision about where a node-scoped automation is written.
open_questions: Does the bench need a correctness axis richer than substring? `--expect` grades work whose answer is checkable that way and nothing else. An automation with a known expected result is a scenario WITH a grader, which is the cheap path; a judge model is the expensive one. Neither is built.

Where does a NODE-scoped automation live? .project/automations.json is project-scoped and the governed writer says so in its name. Two of the three known customers -- restarting this node, verifying this node's catalog -- are node concerns. The sovereign dir is the obvious home, beside config.json, node.json and model-rates.v1.json.

Which cron parser? None exists, this repo is deliberately dependency-light, and cron is subtly easy to get wrong (day-of-week versus day-of-month). Vendoring something tested likely beats hand-rolling, and the choice deserves the same source-and-date discipline every other external dependency here now carries.

rcdc5 as a workspace-scoped automation consumer is BLOCKED on two named pieces, and the blocker is a declared principle rather than an oversight: pending_prompt.rs states P1, `a pending prompt's lifetime is its asker's lifetime, nothing persists`, and nothing resumes a persisted non-terminal effort. Until both change, an automation that waits for an MFA push cannot survive a restart, and 'waiting for a human' is indistinguishable from 'dead'.
